narrative.overview: Everything a future builder sees should feel like a notebook someone carries to a community group: ink drawings, notes in red pencil, a highlighter for what's been chosen, all on dotted paper. The person working is present on the page, and the record at the end reads like the notebook's last pages, written up.
keyCharacteristics: Ink line drawings of people doing things (Open Doodles by Pablo Stanley, CC0), one per group, plus the hero and the empty Make page.
A warm serif for titles (Fraunces) over a highly legible reading face (Atkinson Hyperlegible), with Caveat only for short notes.
Ink is the thing you press. Highlighter marks what is chosen or current. Red pencil is the voice of the person working.
Dotted paper everywhere, with white panels laid on it for working.

rules.name: The One Ink Button Rule
rules.body: Each screen has one filled ink button that matters most. Others are outline pills.

rules.name: The Highlighter Means Chosen Rule
rules.body: Highlighter marks what's current, chosen or ready. It never decorates something the person hasn't picked or reached.

rules.name: The Short Notes Rule
rules.body: Caveat is for notes of a few words. Never a paragraph, a label or a button.

rules.name: The Emphasis Is Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Headline emphasis is a highlighter stroke behind the words, not italic and not a second colour.

rules.name: The Paper Stays Flat Rule
rules.body: Group cards on the board have no box or shadow. Only working panels lift.

dos: Do keep one filled ink button per view.
Do use highlighter only for what is chosen, current or ready.
Do keep pencil notes to a few words.
Do keep the dot grid on the page ground.
Do give every new group a drawing in ink and highlighter.
donts: Don't use red pencil for buttons, links or anything you press.
Don't set paragraphs in Caveat or use it below 20px.
Don't put a box or shadow round board entries.
Don't add a second accent colour. Groups are told apart by their drawings, not tints.
Don't use sparkles, asterisks, glowing gradients or any "magic" AI imagery.
